chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Anger is a kind of madness, because its owner repents; if he does not repent, his madness is confirmed.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on anger as a form of madness?
ai.summary: In this aphorism from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) distinguishes between transient anger and entrenched madness by using the presence of remorse (nadam) as the diagnostic criterion for spiritual health. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on self-reflection (muhasabah) as a mechanism for returning to reason after the temporary loss of control caused by the ego (nafs). The distinction underscores that true sanity is maintained through the capacity to recognize one's faults, whereas persistent lack of remorse signals a deeper, more permanent disorder of the soul.
